Subject: Vendor onboarding: tax documents & EIN mapping for Ellume Tech (multi-entity)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick intro over the phone this morning. Ellume is a group with multiple legal entities and EINs — we have a U.S. operating company (Ellume US, EIN 12-3456789) that handles invoicing for North America and a couple of subsidiaries that invoice in APAC/EU. Procurement at Ellume asked me to send over the tax paperwork required to get a PO in place, and we want to avoid having the PO routed incorrectly to the wrong EIN.

Questions:
- Which EIN should appear on the W-9 for the pilot engagement (we plan to start with a 30-day pilot)?
- Do you accept a bank letter in lieu of notarized W-9 pages for faster processing?
- If remote notarization is required, any preferred providers or templates that Redwood accepts?

I attached the partially completed W-9 our legal team prepared and a bank letter we can provide. If there are other forms (KBA, vendor portal steps) let us know and we’ll turn them around.

Appreciate the help — cc'ing our procurement inbox so they can track.

Best,
Jorge Santos
Head of Finance Ops
Ellume Tech

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: tax documents & EIN mapping for Ellume Tech (multi-entity)

Hi Jorge — thanks for the docs and the summary. Quick answers up front and a proposed path so we can get a PO staged:

1) Which EIN to use
- For procurement and invoicing we need the EIN that will appear on the actual invoice. If Ellume US (EIN 12-3456789) will issue the invoice to Redwood, complete the W-9 for that entity. If a different subsidiary invoices, use that subsidiary's EIN and document the intercompany billing arrangement.

2) Bank letter vs notarized W-9
- We accept a bank letter as supplemental evidence for faster intake, but we still require a completed W-9 for any U.S. invoicing entity. The bank letter can help us clear the vendor faster while full legal validation completes.

3) Remote notarization and alternatives
- Remote notarization is acceptable. If you can't notarize quickly, we accept a certified bank letter (on bank letterhead with banker signature and account masking) or a KYC KBA transcript for higher-risk profiles. For foreign entities, we typically require either a notarized W-8BEN-E or an equivalent local tax residency certificate plus KBA.

Next steps (proposal):
- Please complete and sign the W-9 for Ellume US if that is the invoicing entity (I attached our W9_template.pdf).
- Upload the signed W-9 and the bank letter to the secure intake link (see onboarding-instructions.pdf) or return by email if DocuSign is easier.
- If you prefer DocuSign, I can send an envelope that includes the W-9 and a short authorized-signer attestation; otherwise remote-notary is fine.

Operational note: we'll provision a conditional PO for an initial pilot ($5,000) while verification completes; final PO release requires the signed W-9 and bank evidence on file. Karthik — I’ll hand to you for procurement sequencing and PO creation once Jorge confirms the invoicing entity.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

— Marcus
Procurement Partnerships
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachments: W9_template.pdf, onboarding-instructions.pdf
